Need help planning:

<pasted_content id="1682">

## Summary

Allow users to control how an element moves along its assigned path. Users should be able to set movement speed and tween the speed of the element progresses along the path points, including starting and ending positions. Testing should cover different path lengths, speeds (slow, normal/default, fast), and element types.

## User Story

**As a** team lead or designer, **I want** to be able to tweak my motion path **so that** I can have more control over timing and speed of my animated elements.

## Design Decision | Add to the small edit configuration UI that allows users to set movement speed and path endpoints.

## User Scenario

1. Edit element path
2. Small UI open with Config options
3. User edits speed, start and end to liking.
4. Test reconfigured path with test animation button in small UI
5. Reset or Confirm changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Movement Timing:** Changing the movement speed changes the animation duration accordingly.
- [ ] **Movement Config:** Users can set the movement speed and starting and ending positions of an element on its path.
- [ ] **Smooth Transition:** The element moves smoothly between its configured starting and ending positions.
- [ ] **Setting check:** Movement settings work with paths of different lengths and different supported elements.
- [ ] **Playback:** Configured movement settings are retained when the animation is played again.

## Out of Scope

- Core motion-path system requiring path creation, configuration, and integration with elements.
- Requires animation state, playback controls, timing, and movement execution.
- Adds editing of paths and associated elements without replacing the core motion system.
- Requires motion data to survive save/reopen and work with presentation behavior.

## Head Issue

Issue (#18): Allow elements to have motion </pasted_content id="1682">

19	/** constant speed, not fixed duration — longer paths naturally take longer */
20	const PATH_PLAYBACK_SPEED_PX_PER_SEC = 300;
21
22	type PlaybackState = {
23	  elapsed: number;
24	  totalDuration: number;
25	  originalPositions: Map<string, { x: number; y: number }>;

28	/**
29	 * Drives the basic, fixed-speed "press and hold to preview" path animation.
30	 * Reuses the shared `AnimationController` (a single RAF loop multiplexing
31	 * every concurrently-keyed animation) rather than running its own loop, so
32	 * multiple paths can play back at once with no extra scheduling code.
33	 *
34	 * The target's combined bounding-box center is locked onto the path: at the
35	 * start of playback it's aligned exactly onto the path's first point (in
36	 * absolute scene coordinates), and from there it's displaced by however much
37	 * the path's shape moves at progress `t` — so the target visibly rides the
38	 * drawn dashed line rather than merely replaying its shape from wherever the
39	 * target happens to currently sit.
40	 *
41	 * Per-frame mutations are explicitly scheduled as `CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER`
42	 * on every tick (not left to the default `EVENTUALLY`), since an animation
43	 * can run for seconds, during which an unrelated user action could schedule
44	 * an `IMMEDIATELY` capture that would otherwise sweep a mid-flight frame into
45	 * an unrelated undo entry.
46	 */
47	export class PathPlaybackController {
48	  constructor(private app: App) {}
49
50	  isPlaying(path: ExcalidrawPathElement): boolean {
51	    return AnimationController.running(playbackKey(path.id));
52	  }
53
54	  start(path: ExcalidrawPathElement, targets: NonDeletedExcalidrawElement[]) {
55	    const key = playbackKey(path.id);
56
57	    if (AnimationController.running(key) || targets.length === 0) {
58	      return;
59	    }
60
61	    const elementsMap = this.app.scene.getNonDeletedElementsMap();
62	    const globalPoints = getPathGlobalSamplePoints(path, elementsMap);
63	    const length = getPathLength(globalPoints);
64	    const totalDuration = Math.max(
65	      (length / PATH_PLAYBACK_SPEED_PX_PER_SEC) * 1000,
66	      1,
67	    );
68
69	    const originalPositions = new Map<string, { x: number; y: number }>();
70	    for (const target of targets) {
71	      originalPositions.set(target.id, { x: target.x, y: target.y });
72	      const boundText = getBoundTextElement(target, elementsMap);
73	      if (boundText) {
74	        originalPositions.set(boundText.id, {
75	          x: boundText.x,
76	          y: boundText.y,
77	        });
78	      }
79	    }
80
81	    // one-time alignment so the target's combined bounding-box center lands
82	    // exactly on the path's first point (in absolute scene coordinates) at
83	    // t=0, then stays glued to the path's shape as it progresses. In the
84	    // common case this is already ~(0,0), since the target was snapped onto
85	    // the path the moment it was confirmed (see actionFinalize.tsx) — this
86	    // is a safety net for whenever that's no longer true (e.g. the path or
87	    // target was repositioned since), so playback still starts glued to the
88	    // line rather than replaying the path's shape from wherever the target
89	    // happens to currently sit.
90	    const alignmentOffset = getPathAlignmentOffset(path, targets, elementsMap);
91
92	    AnimationController.start<PlaybackState>(key, ({ deltaTime, state }) => {
93	      const next: PlaybackState = state
94	        ? { ...state, elapsed: state.elapsed + deltaTime }
95	        : { elapsed: 0, totalDuration, originalPositions };
96
97	      const t = Math.min(next.elapsed / next.totalDuration, 1);
98	      const { x: dx, y: dy } = getPointAtProgress(globalPoints, t);
99	      const [startDx, startDy] = globalPoints[0] ?? [0, 0];
100	      const totalDeltaX = dx - startDx + alignmentOffset.x;
101	      const totalDeltaY = dy - startDy + alignmentOffset.y;
102
103	      const liveOriginalPositions = new Map(
104	        [...next.originalPositions].filter(([id]) =>
105	          this.app.scene.getNonDeletedElement(id),
106	        ),
107	      );
108
109	      if (liveOriginalPositions.size === 0) {
110	        return null;
111	      }
112
113	      for (const [id, orig] of liveOriginalPositions) {
114	        const element = this.app.scene.getNonDeletedElement(id);
115	        if (!element) {
116	          continue;
117	        }
118	        this.app.scene.mutateElement(
119	          element,
120	          {
121	            x: orig.x + totalDeltaX,
122	            y: orig.y + totalDeltaY,
123	          },
124	          { informMutation: true, isDragging: true },
125	        );
126	      }
127	      this.app.scheduleNeverCapture();
128
129	      if (t >= 1) {
130	        for (const [id, orig] of liveOriginalPositions) {
131	          const element = this.app.scene.getNonDeletedElement(id);
132	          if (element) {
133	            this.app.scene.mutateElement(element, orig, {
134	              informMutation: true,
135	              isDragging: false,
136	            });
137	          }
138	        }
139	        this.app.scheduleNeverCapture();
140	        return null;
141	      }
142
143	      return next;
144	    });
145	  }
146

31	export const getPathTargetElements = (
32	  path: ExcalidrawPathElement,
33	  elements: ElementsMapOrArray,

64	  for (const candidate of arrayToMap(elements).values()) {
65	    if (!isPathElement(candidate) || candidate.isDeleted) {
66	      continue;
67	    }
68	    if (
69	      candidate.targetElementId === element.id ||
70	      (candidate.targetGroupId !== null &&
71	        element.groupIds.includes(candidate.targetGroupId))
72	    ) {
73	      paths.push(candidate as NonDeleted<ExcalidrawPathElement>);
74	    }
75	  }
76	  return paths;
77	};
78
79	/**
80	 * The path's travel polyline (see `getPathSamplePoints`) in absolute scene
81	 * coordinates, with the path's rotation applied — i.e. exactly the line the
82	 * user sees on canvas, whether the path has been moved, resized, rotated or
83	 * curved.
84	 */
85	export const getPathGlobalSamplePoints = (
86	  path: ExcalidrawPathElement,
87	  elementsMap: ElementsMap,
88	): GlobalPoint[] => {
89	  const [, , , , cx, cy] = getElementAbsoluteCoords(path, elementsMap);
90	  const center = pointFrom<GlobalPoint>(cx, cy);
91	  return getPathSamplePoints(path).map(([x, y]) =>
92	    pointRotateRads(
93	      pointFrom<GlobalPoint>(path.x + x, path.y + y),
94	      center,
95	      path.angle,
96	    ),
97	  );
98	};

100	/**
101	 * The translation that would snap `targets`' combined bounding-box center
102	 * onto the path's (rotated) first point in absolute scene coordinates. Used
103	 * both to snap a path's target to it the moment the path is confirmed or an
104	 * edit session is committed (so they sit together at rest, not just
105	 * mid-animation) and, identically, as the playback alignment at progress 0 —
106	 * the two must use the same formula so the resting position and the start
107	 * of the animation coincide exactly.
108	 */
109	export const getPathAlignmentOffset = (
110	  path: ExcalidrawPathElement,
111	  targets: readonly ExcalidrawElement[],
112	  elementsMap: ElementsMap,
113	): { x: number; y: number } => {
114	  if (targets.length === 0) {
115	    return { x: 0, y: 0 };
116	  }
117
118	  const [minX, minY, maxX, maxY] = getCommonBounds(targets, elementsMap);
119	  const referenceCenter = { x: (minX + maxX) / 2, y: (minY + maxY) / 2 };
120	  const [startX, startY] = getPathGlobalSamplePoints(path, elementsMap)[0] ?? [
121	    path.x,
122	    path.y,
123	  ];
124
125	  return {
126	    x: startX - referenceCenter.x,
127	    y: startY - referenceCenter.y,
128	  };
129	};
130
131	/**
132	 * Moves the path's live target(s) — and their bound text — so their combined
133	 * center sits on the path's start point. No-op when already aligned.
134	 */
135	export const snapPathTargetsToStart = (
136	  path: ExcalidrawPathElement,
137	  scene: Scene,
138	) => {
139	  const elementsMap = scene.getNonDeletedElementsMap();
140	  const targets = getPathTargetElements(path, elementsMap);
141	  const offset = getPathAlignmentOffset(path, targets, elementsMap);
142	  if (offset.x === 0 && offset.y === 0) {
143	    return;
144	  }
145	  for (const target of targets) {
146	    scene.mutateElement(target, {
147	      x: target.x + offset.x,
148	      y: target.y + offset.y,
149	    });
150	    const boundText = getBoundTextElement(target, elementsMap);
151	    if (boundText) {
152	      scene.mutateElement(boundText, {
153	        x: boundText.x + offset.x,
154	        y: boundText.y + offset.y,
155	      });
156	    }
157	  }
158	};
159
160	/** Total euclidean length of the polyline described by `points`. */
161	export const getPathLength = <P extends LocalPoint | GlobalPoint>(
162	  points: readonly P[],
163	): number => {
164	  let length = 0;
165	  for (let i = 1; i < points.length; i++) {
166	    length += pointDistance(points[i - 1], points[i]);
167	  }
168	  return length;
169	};
170
171	/**
172	 * Walks the polyline's segments by cumulative length to find the point at
173	 * progress `t` (0..1) along it, interpolating within the containing segment.
174	 * `t` is clamped to [0, 1]; a path with fewer than 2 points returns its only
175	 * point (or the origin if empty).
176	 */
177	export const getPointAtProgress = <P extends LocalPoint | GlobalPoint>(
178	  points: readonly P[],
179	  t: number,
180	): { x: number; y: number } => {
181	  if (points.length === 0) {
182	    return { x: 0, y: 0 };
183	  }
184	  if (points.length === 1) {
185	    return { x: points[0][0], y: points[0][1] };
186	  }
187
188	  const clampedT = Math.min(Math.max(t, 0), 1);
189	  const totalLength = getPathLength(points);
190
191	  if (totalLength === 0) {
192	    return { x: points[0][0], y: points[0][1] };
193	  }
194
195	  const targetLength = clampedT * totalLength;
196	  let traveled = 0;
197
198	  for (let i = 1; i < points.length; i++) {
199	    const segmentLength = pointDistance(points[i - 1], points[i]);
200	    if (traveled + segmentLength >= targetLength || i === points.length - 1) {
201	      const segmentT =
202	        segmentLength === 0 ? 0 : (targetLength - traveled) / segmentLength;
203	      const [x0, y0] = points[i - 1];
204	      const [x1, y1] = points[i];
205	      return {
206	        x: x0 + (x1 - x0) * segmentT,
207	        y: y0 + (y1 - y0) * segmentT,
208	      };
209	    }
210	    traveled += segmentLength;
211	  }
212
213	  const last = points[points.length - 1];
214	  return { x: last[0], y: last[1] };
215	};
216

1	import {
2	  bezierEquation,
3	  curveCatmullRomCubicApproxPoints,
4	} from "@excalidraw/math";
5
6	import type { LocalPoint } from "@excalidraw/math";
7
8	import type { ExcalidrawPathElement } from "./types";
9
10	/** bezier samples taken per segment when a path is curved */
11	const CURVE_SAMPLES_PER_SEGMENT = 16;
12
13	/**
14	 * The polyline a path actually travels along, in the path's local
15	 * coordinates: its raw `points` when straight, or a dense sampling of the
16	 * smooth curve through those points when `roundness` is set.
17	 *
18	 * The curve is a Catmull-Rom spline at tension 0.5, whose bezier control
19	 * points (p1 + (p2 - p0) / 6) are identical to roughjs's `curve()` at its
20	 * default tightness — which `generateLinearCollisionShape` uses for curved
21	 * paths — so rendering, playback, hit-testing and the linear editor's
22	 * midpoints all agree on the same geometry.
23	 *
24	 * Kept free of other element-package imports so bounds/linearElementEditor
25	 * can depend on it without creating an import cycle.
26	 */
27	export const getPathSamplePoints = (
28	  path: Pick<ExcalidrawPathElement, "points" | "roundness">,
29	): readonly LocalPoint[] => {
30	  if (!path.roundness || path.points.length <= 2) {
31	    return path.points;
32	  }
33
34	  const curves = curveCatmullRomCubicApproxPoints(path.points as LocalPoint[]);
35	  if (!curves) {
36	    return path.points;
37	  }
38
39	  const samples: LocalPoint[] = [path.points[0]];
40	  for (const c of curves) {
41	    for (let step = 1; step <= CURVE_SAMPLES_PER_SEGMENT; step++) {
42	      samples.push(bezierEquation(c, step / CURVE_SAMPLES_PER_SEGMENT));
43	    }
44	  }
45	  return samples;
46	};
47

commit 2dfebf8b03aacf41954235ed76500159cc0b92e7
Author: Anthony Williams <aawilliams01@wm.edu>
Date:   Sat Oct 3 23:08:39 2026 -0400

    feat: add motion path tool (#45)

    Adds a new first-class "path" element type for defining a motion
    trajectory that a selected element or group can follow, per issue #45
    (head issue #18).

    - Path tool: click a target element/group, then click to place a
      start point, optional midpoints, and an end point; finish by
      clicking back near the last point or pressing Enter/Escape. Reuses
      the existing multi-point line drawing/editing machinery.
    - Points-only editing during creation; a path is intentionally not
      re-editable, resizable, or rotatable after confirm, since its
      points, the snap-to-target alignment, and playback math all read
      directly from its unrotated local points/x/y.
    - On confirm, the target is snapped so its bounding-box center sits
      on the path's start point, and dragging either the path or its
      target moves both together, keeping them visually coincident at
      rest and not just mid-animation.
    - Press-and-hold (~1s) on the target plays a fixed-speed animation
      along the path via the existing shared AnimationController, with
      the target snapping back to its resting position afterward;
      concurrent paths on different targets animate independently.
    - Dashed-line + waypoint-dot rendering on canvas and in SVG export;
      restore/bounds/collision support so paths persist and hit-test
      correctly, including when later points extend above/left of the
      path's start.

    Covered by new unit and end-to-end tests in
    packages/element/tests/path.test.ts and
    packages/excalidraw/tests/pathElement.test.tsx.

    Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

185	 * Re-opens a confirmed motion path for editing: point editing via the

187	 * kept visible for the path while editing (see hasBoundingBox). The path and

202	      !selectedElements[0].locked &&

235	          // shallow copy is enough)

Author: Anthony Williams <aawilliams01@wm.edu>
Date:   Tue Oct 6 23:41:40 2026 -0400

    feat(editor): edit motion path and element after configuration (#48)

    - Right-click (or double-click) a motion path -> "Edit motion path" to
      move/add/delete points, move/resize/rotate the path, and toggle it
      between straight and curved, from a small floating toolbar with
      Test animation / Curved / Reject / Done.
    - Delete removes selected points (min 2); with none selected it rejects
      the session. Clicking off, Esc or Done confirms and snaps the element
      onto the path's start.
    - Re-enable resize/rotate for paths (rescale points on resize); playback,
      bounds, hit-testing and SVG export follow the rotated/curved path.
    - Re-snap the element onto the path start after any resize/rotate of the
      path or its element.
    - Reject restores a copied snapshot (scene edits mutate in place).

    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

11	    | { id: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>; type: "timeout" }

22	  static start<R extends object>(key: string, animation: Animation<R>) {
23	    if (AnimationController.animations.has(key)) {

25	    }

46	    }

50	        id: requestAnimationFrame(AnimationController.tick),
51	        type: "raf",
52	      };

54	      AnimationController.scheduledFrame = {
55	        id: setTimeout(AnimationController.tick, 0),
56	        type: "timeout",

67	      cancelAnimationFrame(AnimationController.scheduledFrame.id);
68	    } else {
69	      clearTimeout(AnimationController.scheduledFrame.id);
70	    }
71
72	    AnimationController.scheduledFrame = null;
73	  }
74
75	  private static cancelScheduledFrameIfIdle() {
76	    if (AnimationController.animations.size > 0) {
77	      return false;
78	    }

_**Agent - sidechain (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-08 03:51:33Z)**_

I found every part of the motion path feature. There is no per-path speed, duration, easing or start/end timing anywhere, and no presentation mode is wired up. Playback runs at one fixed speed and is started two ways: by holding the pointer on the target element, or by the toolbar's "Test animation" button.

Paths below are relative to `C:\Users\tonyw\projects\draw_main_proj\excalidraw\packages\`.

Relevant commits:

- **`2dfebf8b` (#45, under head issue #18):** added the `path` element type, the path tool, the playback engine, restore support and the first tests.
- **`e91ec3d9` (#48):** added editing after configuration (an action file, a toolbar component, the `motionPathEditor` app state), curved paths, path resize/rotate and `pathEditing.test.tsx`.

## 1. Data model

- **Element type.** `element/src/types.ts:392-400` declares a first-class element type. It is not stored in `customData`, and `customData` is not used by this feature at all.
  ```ts
  export type ExcalidrawPathElement = _ExcalidrawElementBase &
    Readonly<{
      type: "path";
      points: readonly LocalPoint[];
      targetElementId: string | null; // mutually exclusive with targetGroupId
      targetGroupId: GroupId | null; // resolved once at creation time
    }>;
  ```
  - It is added to the `ExcalidrawElement` union.
  - It is deliberately separate from `ExcalidrawLinearElement`, so paths have no bindings or arrowheads.
  - "Curved" means `roundness` (from the base element) is non-null, `{type: ROUNDNESS.PROPORTIONAL_RADIUS}`.
  - Rotation is the base `angle` field.
- **Linking.** The path points to its target; the element itself stores nothing. Lookups are in `element/src/path.ts`:
  - `getPathTargetElements(path, elements)` (lines 31-51) resolves the target element or group members. It returns `[]` if the target was deleted.
  - `getPathsTargetingElement(element, elements)` (lines 59-77) is the reverse lookup. Playback uses the first match.
- **Other places:**
  - Constructor: `newPathElement` in `element/src/newElement.ts`.
  - Type check: `isPathElement` in `element/src/typeChecks.ts`.
  - Tool type: `TOOL_TYPE.path` in `common/src/constants.ts`.
  - `PATH_PLAYBACK_HOLD_MS = 1000` is also in `common/src/constants.ts`.
  - `ToolType` includes `"path"` in `excalidraw/types.ts`.
- **App state** (`excalidraw/types.ts`, defaults in `excalidraw/appState.ts`; neither field is persisted or tracked by undo):
  - `pendingPathTarget`: the target chosen by the path tool's first click.
  - `motionPathEditor` (#48): `{ pathId, original: ExcalidrawPathElement, originalPositions: Record<id,{x,y}> } | null`.
  - `multiElement` was widened to accept path elements.

## 2. Animation and playback engine

- **`excalidraw/pathPlayback.ts`: `PathPlaybackController`**
  - Line 20: `PATH_PLAYBACK_SPEED_PX_PER_SEC = 300`. Speed is constant, so a longer path takes longer.
  - `start(path, targets)` (lines 54-145) works like this:
    - It gets `globalPoints = getPathGlobalSamplePoints(path, elementsMap)`.
    - `totalDuration = max(length/300*1000, 1)` ms.
    - It snapshots the target's and any bound text's `originalPositions` and computes a one-time `getPathAlignmentOffset`.
    - Each frame it uses `AnimationController.start(key, ({deltaTime,state}) => ...)`. Timing is linear (`t = elapsed/totalDuration`, no easing). It calls `getPointAtProgress(globalPoints, t)`, moves the targets with `scene.mutateElement(..., {isDragging:true})`, then calls `app.scheduleNeverCapture()` so animation frames never land in undo history.
    - At `t>=1` it puts the targets back where they started.
  - `startForPath(path)` (line 148, from #48) plays the path against its current targets.
  - `isPlaying` and `cancel` use the key `path-playback-${id}`.
- **`excalidraw/renderer/animation.ts`: `AnimationController`** is the shared static loop. It runs on requestAnimationFrame, or `setTimeout(0)` when render throttling is off (that is the case in tests). Main methods: `start` (line 22), `tick` (line 84, computes `deltaTime` from `performance.now()`), `running` (line 118), `cancel` (line 122).
- **`element/src/path.ts` (geometry):**
  - `getPathGlobalSamplePoints` (lines 85-98): sample points converted to scene coordinates with the path's rotation applied.
  - `getPathAlignmentOffset` (lines 109-129): offset that puts the targets' combined bounding-box center on the path's start point.
  - `snapPathTargetsToStart(path, scene)` (lines 135-158).
  - `getPathLength` (lines 161-169).
  - `getPointAtProgress(points, t)` (lines 177-215): walks the polyline by distance travelled and interpolates linearly within the segment.
- **`element/src/pathSamples.ts`: `getPathSamplePoints`** returns the raw points when the path is straight. When `roundness` is set it returns a Catmull-Rom curve built from bezier segments, 16 samples per segment.
- **Triggers in `excalidraw/components/App.tsx`:**
  - Line 775: `pathPlayback = new PathPlaybackController(this)`.
  - Line 8409 calls `armPathPlaybackIfApplicable`. That function (lines 10225-10261) only works with the selection tool. If the pressed element has a path, a timer starts and fires after `PATH_PLAYBACK_HOLD_MS`.
  - The hold is cancelled if the pointer moves past the drag threshold (around line 10500) or on pointer-up (around line 11428, `clearPathPlaybackArm`).
  - The toolbar's Test button calls `this.pathPlayback.startForPath(...)` (lines 2439-2443).
  - No presentation or play-all mode exists. `presentationIcon` in `components/icons.tsx:2548` is only an icon definition.

## 3. The #48 edit UI

- **`excalidraw/components/MotionPathEditToolbar.tsx`** (107 lines; styles in `MotionPathEditToolbar.scss`)
  - Props: `{path, elementsMap, onTestAnimation}`.
  - It is placed at the path's top-right corner plus `HANDLE_CLEARANCE=24`.
  - It hides while a context menu is open, an element is being created, resized or rotated, while dragging, or in view mode.
  - Buttons (test IDs):
    - `motion-path-test`: calls `onTestAnimation`.
    - `motion-path-curve`: runs `actionToggleMotionPathCurve`, with `aria-pressed` set when curved.
    - `motion-path-reject`: runs `actionRejectMotionPathEdit`.
    - `motion-path-done`: runs `actionFinishMotionPathEdit`.
  - The container's test ID is `motion-path-edit-toolbar`.
  - It is rendered in `App.tsx:2432-2445` when exactly one path is selected and `motionPathEditor.pathId` matches it.
- **`excalidraw/actions/actionMotionPathEditor.tsx`:**
  - `actionEditMotionPath` (lines 190-243): available when exactly one unlocked path is selected. It sets `selectedLinearElement = new LinearElementEditor(path, map, true)` and stores the `motionPathEditor` snapshot (a shallow copy `{...path}` plus the targets' starting positions).
  - `actionFinishMotionPathEdit` (lines 62-105): snaps the targets onto the path start and exits edit mode.
  - `rejectMotionPathEdit` and `actionRejectMotionPathEdit` (lines 113-153): restore x, y, width, height, angle, points and roundness, plus the target positions.
  - `actionToggleMotionPathCurve` (lines 155-182).
- **How editing opens:**
  - The context menu entry is `actionEditMotionPath` (`App.tsx:13659`).
  - Double-clicking a selected path also opens it (`App.tsx:6959-6963`).
- **How editing ends:** the session is committed automatically in `componentDidUpdate` (`App.tsx:3716-3733`) when the editor goes away, through a deferred `setTimeout`. That covers clicking off, Esc and Done.
- **Related wiring:**
  - `actions/actionFinalize.tsx:169-187`: point edits during a session stay in edit mode.
  - `actions/actionDeleteSelected.tsx`: Delete with no points selected rejects the session, and a path keeps at least 2 points.
  - `renderer/interactiveScene.ts:~1861`: keeps the bounding box and handles visible while editing.
  - `App.tsx:12026-12043`: re-snaps targets after resizing or rotating the path or its target.
  - Labels are under `labels.pathEditor.*` in `locales/en.json`: edit, testAnimation, curved, straight, reject, done.
  - Action names are added in `actions/types.ts` and exported from `actions/index.ts`.

## 4. Persistence

- **`excalidraw/data/restore.ts`:**
  - Line 228: `AllowedExcalidrawActiveTools.path = true`.
  - The `case "path"` branch (lines 749-780) restores the points and shifts them so the first point is at 0,0 (`LinearElementEditor.getNormalizeElementPointsAndCoords`). It sets `targetElementId`/`targetGroupId ?? null` and `...getSizeFromPoints(points)`. A target that no longer exists is left as-is.
- `roundness` and `angle` come back through the base `restoreElementWithProperties`.
- Serialization has no special handling; the path is an ordinary element in JSON.
- SVG export: `renderer/staticSvgScene.ts:386` draws the path as a dashed line with dots at each point.

## 5. Tests

- **`element/tests/path.test.ts`**: unit tests for the geometry helpers, absolute coordinates, alignment offset, transform handles and resizing, curved and rotated sampling, and the target lookups.
- **`excalidraw/tests/pathElement.test.tsx`**: drawing with the path tool, and dragging the path and target together.
- **`excalidraw/tests/pathEditing.test.tsx`**: the #48 tests (423 lines), covering entering edit mode, point editing, curve toggle, Test animation, confirm/reject, transforms, and re-snapping. Its patterns:
  - `render(<Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally />)` with `reseed(7)`.
  - `API.createElement({type:"path", points, targetElementId, ...getSizeFromPoints(points)})` (supported in `tests/helpers/api.ts` around lines 211-253 and 391).
  - `API.setElements`, plus `Pointer`/`Keyboard`/`UI.clickOnTestId` from `tests/helpers/ui`.
  - `mouse.rightClickAt` followed by `queryByTestId(UI.queryContextMenu()!, "editMotionPath")`.
  - A `flushDeferred()` helper (`act` + `setTimeout 0`) lets the deferred commit run.
  - Playback is checked with `h.app.pathPlayback.isPlaying(...)` and then `cancel(...)`.
  - Expected values are written as literals, because scene edits change element objects in place.
- Snapshots that changed: `excalidraw/tests/__snapshots__/{contextmenu,history,regressionTests}.test.tsx.snap` and `utils/tests/__snapshots__/export.test.ts.snap`.

30	 * Reuses the shared `AnimationController` (a single RAF loop multiplexing

32	 * multiple paths can play back at once with no extra scheduling code.

42	 * on every tick (not left to the default `EVENTUALLY`), since an animation

44	 * an `IMMEDIATELY` capture that would otherwise sweep a mid-flight frame into
45	 * an unrelated undo entry.

47	export class PathPlaybackController {
48	  constructor(private app: App) {}
49
50	  isPlaying(path: ExcalidrawPathElement): boolean {
51	    return AnimationController.running(playbackKey(path.id));

53

59	    }
60

62	    const globalPoints = getPathGlobalSamplePoints(path, elementsMap);
63	    const length = getPathLength(globalPoints);
64	    const totalDuration = Math.max(
65	      (length / PATH_PLAYBACK_SPEED_PX_PER_SEC) * 1000,
66	      1,
67	    );
68
69	    const originalPositions = new Map<string, { x: number; y: number }>();
70	    for (const target of targets) {
71	      originalPositions.set(target.id, { x: target.x, y: target.y });
72	      const boundText = getBoundTextElement(target, elementsMap);
73	      if (boundText) {
74	        originalPositions.set(boundText.id, {
75	          x: boundText.x,
76	          y: boundText.y,

78	      }
79	    }

82	    // exactly on the path's first point (in absolute scene coordinates) at

<tool-use data-tool-type="generic" data-tool-name="AskUserQuestion"><details>

<summary>Tool use: **AskUserQuestion**</summary>
**How should users set movement speed in the edit toolbar?**

Options:

- **Presets + multiplier (Recommended)** - Slow / Normal / Fast buttons mapping to 0.5x / 1x / 2x of the current 300 px/s base. Simple, matches the issue's test cases, and longer paths still take longer.
- **Numeric slider** - Continuous speed multiplier slider (e.g. 0.25x–4x), with Normal at 1x.
- **Fixed duration (seconds)** - User enters total seconds; path length no longer affects timing.

**How should start and end positions on the path be chosen?**

Options:

- **Percent of path (Recommended)** - Two sliders, start 0–100% and end 0–100% of path length (start < end). Works on curved paths and any length.
- **Snap to path points** - Pick a starting and ending vertex index. Simpler, but coarse and awkward on curves.
- **Drag markers on canvas** - Draggable start/end handles drawn on the path itself. Nicest UX, significantly more work in the renderer and pointer handlers.

**The issue says to 'tween the speed'. Should an easing option be included?**

Options:

- **Yes, easing presets (Recommended)** - Linear (default), Ease in, Ease out, Ease in-out applied to progress t.
- **No, linear only** - Keep constant speed; just speed + start/end.

**Answer:** Presets + multiplier (Recommended), Percent of path (Recommended), Yes, easing presets (Recommended)

## Context

Paths (#45) currently play back at a fixed 300 px/s, linearly, over the full path (`packages/excalidraw/pathPlayback.ts`). Issue #46 asks users to control _how_ the target moves: speed, easing ("tween"), and a start/end section of the path, all from the #48 edit toolbar (`MotionPathEditToolbar.tsx`), testable with "Test animation", revertible with Reject, and kept after save/reload.

Decisions made with the user:

- **Speed**: Slow / Normal / Fast presets → multipliers 0.5 / 1 / 2 on the 300 px/s base. Longer paths still take longer.
- **Start/End**: percent of path length (0–100%), two range sliders, `start < end`.
- **Easing**: Linear (default), Ease in, Ease out, Ease in-out.

## 1. Data model — `packages/element/src/types.ts`

Add one nested, readonly config to `ExcalidrawPathElement` so snapshot/reject/restore treat it as one value:

```ts
export type PathMotionEasing = "linear" | "easeIn" | "easeOut" | "easeInOut";
export type PathMotionConfig = Readonly<{
  speed: number; // multiplier on base px/s, 1 = normal
  start: number; // 0..1 fraction of path length
  end: number; // 0..1, > start
  easing: PathMotionEasing;
}>;
// on ExcalidrawPathElement:
motion: PathMotionConfig;
```

- `newPathElement` (`packages/element/src/newElement.ts`): accept optional `motion`, default `DEFAULT_PATH_MOTION`.
- `tests/helpers/api.ts` (path branch ~L211-253): pass through `motion`.

## 2. Geometry + easing — `packages/element/src/path.ts`

- Add `getPathMotionEasing(easing) => (t) => number`. Reuse `easeOut` from `packages/common/src/utils.ts:203` for "easeOut"; add `easeIn` (t³) and `easeInOut` (cubic) next to it in common utils.
- Add `normalizePathMotion(motion?)`: fills defaults, clamps start/end to [0,1], enforces `end - start >= PATH_MOTION_MIN_SPAN`, speed > 0. Used by restore and actions.
- Change `getPathAlignmentOffset` (L109-129) to anchor the target's bbox center on `getPointAtProgress(globalPoints, path.motion.start)` instead of point 0. When `start` changes, also shift targets by the new `getPathAlignmentOffset` (same logic as Finish L76-100; pull that into a small shared helper `alignTargetsToPathStart(elements, path)`) so the target visibly sits at the new start while editing. `captureUpdate: IMMEDIATELY`.
- `rejectMotionPathEdit` (L126-134): also restore `motion: original.motion`. The snapshot in `actionEditMotionPath` already shallow-copies the path, so `original.motion` is captured.

  - Start/End sliders update `motion`; target re-snaps to the start point; end ≤ start is clamped.

  - Reject restores the original `motion`; Done keeps it.
  - Playback with a configured section starts at `start` point and the target returns to rest after finishing; playing twice gives identical results.
  - Element types: rectangle, ellipse, text, and a group target (`targetGroupId`).
- `restore` test: legacy path without `motion` gets defaults; out-of-range values clamped.
- Run `yarn test:update` (contextmenu/history/regression/export snapshots will change because of the new `motion` field).

1. `yarn test:typecheck`

161	export const getPathLength = <P extends LocalPoint | GlobalPoint>(
162	  points: readonly P[],

177	export const getPointAtProgress = <P extends LocalPoint | GlobalPoint>(
178	  points: readonly P[],
179	  t: number,

181	  if (points.length === 0) {
182	    return { x: 0, y: 0 };
183	  }
184	  if (points.length === 1) {
185	    return { x: points[0][0], y: points[0][1] };

188	  const clampedT = Math.min(Math.max(t, 0), 1);
189	  const totalLength = getPathLength(points);

192	    return { x: points[0][0], y: points[0][1] };
193	  }

195	  const targetLength = clampedT * totalLength;
196	  let traveled = 0;
197
198	  for (let i = 1; i < points.length; i++) {
199	    const segmentLength = pointDistance(points[i - 1], points[i]);
200	    if (traveled + segmentLength >= targetLength || i === points.length - 1) {
201	      const segmentT =
202	        segmentLength === 0 ? 0 : (targetLength - traveled) / segmentLength;
203	      const [x0, y0] = points[i - 1];
204	      const [x1, y1] = points[i];
205	      return {
206	        x: x0 + (x1 - x0) * segmentT,
207	        y: y0 + (y1 - y0) * segmentT,
208	      };
209	    }
210	    traveled += segmentLength;

```typescript
import {
  PATH_MOTION_MIN_SPAN,
  clamp,
  easeIn,
  easeInOut,
  easeOut,
} from "@excalidraw/common";

import type { PathMotionConfig, PathMotionEasing } from "./types";

export const DEFAULT_PATH_MOTION: PathMotionConfig = {
  speed: 1,
  start: 0,
  end: 1,
  easing: "linear",
};

const PATH_MOTION_EASINGS: Record<PathMotionEasing, (t: number) => number> = {
  linear: (t) => t,
  easeIn,
  easeOut,
  easeInOut,
};

export const isPathMotionEasing = (value: unknown): value is PathMotionEasing =>
  typeof value === "string" && value in PATH_MOTION_EASINGS;

export const getPathMotionEasing = (easing: PathMotionEasing) =>
  PATH_MOTION_EASINGS[easing] ?? PATH_MOTION_EASINGS.linear;

/**
 * Fills in defaults for a (possibly partial, legacy or hand-edited) motion
 * config and clamps it into a playable range: speed > 0, start/end within
 * [0, 1] and at least `PATH_MOTION_MIN_SPAN` apart.
 */
export const normalizePathMotion = (
  motion?: Partial<PathMotionConfig> | null,
): PathMotionConfig => {
  const speed =
    typeof motion?.speed === "number" &&
    Number.isFinite(motion.speed) &&
    motion.speed > 0
      ? motion.speed
      : DEFAULT_PATH_MOTION.speed;

  const rawStart = Number.isFinite(motion?.start)
    ? motion!.start!
    : DEFAULT_PATH_MOTION.start;
  const rawEnd = Number.isFinite(motion?.end)
    ? motion!.end!
    : DEFAULT_PATH_MOTION.end;

  const start = clamp(rawStart, 0, 1 - PATH_MOTION_MIN_SPAN);
  const end = clamp(rawEnd, start + PATH_MOTION_MIN_SPAN, 1);

  return {
    speed,
    start,
    end,
    easing: isPathMotionEasing(motion?.easing)
      ? motion!.easing!
      : DEFAULT_PATH_MOTION.easing,
  };
};
```

4	  deltaTime: number;
5	  state?: R;
6	}) => R | null | undefined;
7
8	export class AnimationController {
9	  private static scheduledFrame:
10	    | { id: ReturnType<typeof requestAnimationFrame>; type: "raf" }
11	    | { id: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>; type: "timeout" }
12	    | null = null;
13	  private static animations = new Map<
14	    string,
15	    {
16	      animation: Animation<any>;
17	      lastTime: number;
18	      state: any;
19	    }
20	  >();
21
22	  static start<R extends object>(key: string, animation: Animation<R>) {
23	    if (AnimationController.animations.has(key)) {
24	      return;
25	    }
26
27	    const initialState = animation({
28	      deltaTime: 0,
29	      state: undefined,
30	    });
31
32	    if (initialState) {
33	      AnimationController.animations.set(key, {
34	        animation,
35	        lastTime: 0,
36	        state: initialState,
37	      });
38
39	      AnimationController.scheduleNextFrame();
40	    }
41	  }
42
43	  private static scheduleNextFrame() {
44	    if (AnimationController.scheduledFrame) {
45	      return;
46	    }
47
48	    if (isRenderThrottlingEnabled()) {
49	      AnimationController.scheduledFrame = {
50	        id: requestAnimationFrame(AnimationController.tick),
51	        type: "raf",
52	      };
53	    } else {
54	      AnimationController.scheduledFrame = {
55	        id: setTimeout(AnimationController.tick, 0),
56	        type: "timeout",
57	      };
58	    }
59	  }
60
61	  private static cancelScheduledFrame() {
62	    if (!AnimationController.scheduledFrame) {
63	      return;
64	    }
65
66	    if (AnimationController.scheduledFrame.type === "raf") {
67	      cancelAnimationFrame(AnimationController.scheduledFrame.id);
68	    } else {
69	      clearTimeout(AnimationController.scheduledFrame.id);
70	    }
71
72	    AnimationController.scheduledFrame = null;
73	  }
74
75	  private static cancelScheduledFrameIfIdle() {
76	    if (AnimationController.animations.size > 0) {
77	      return false;
78	    }
79
80	    AnimationController.cancelScheduledFrame();
81	    return true;
82	  }
83
84	  private static tick() {
85	    AnimationController.scheduledFrame = null;
86
87	    if (AnimationController.animations.size > 0) {
88	      for (const [key, animation] of AnimationController.animations) {
89	        const now = performance.now();
90	        const deltaTime =
91	          animation.lastTime === 0 ? 0 : now - animation.lastTime;
92
93	        const state = animation.animation({
94	          deltaTime,
95	          state: animation.state,
96	        });
97
98	        if (!state) {
99	          AnimationController.animations.delete(key);
100
101	          if (AnimationController.cancelScheduledFrameIfIdle()) {
102	            return;
103	          }
104	        } else {
105	          animation.lastTime = now;
106	          animation.state = state;
107	        }
108	      }
109
110	      if (AnimationController.cancelScheduledFrameIfIdle()) {
111	        return;
112	      }
113
114	      AnimationController.scheduleNextFrame();
115	    }
116	  }
117
118	  static running(key: string) {
119	    return AnimationController.animations.has(key);
120	  }
121
122	  static cancel(key: string) {
123	    AnimationController.animations.delete(key);
124	    AnimationController.cancelScheduledFrameIfIdle();
125	  }
126
127	  static reset() {
128	    AnimationController.animations.clear();
129	    AnimationController.cancelScheduledFrame();
130	  }
131	}

import { pointFrom, type LocalPoint } from "@excalidraw/math";
import { arrayToMap } from "@excalidraw/common";
import { API } from "@excalidraw/excalidraw/tests/helpers/api";

import { getPathAlignmentOffset } from "../src/path";
import {
  DEFAULT_PATH_MOTION,
  getPathMotionEasing,
  normalizePathMotion,
} from "../src/pathMotion";

import type { PathMotionEasing } from "../src/types";

describe("getPathMotionEasing", () => {
  const easings: PathMotionEasing[] = [
    "linear",
    "easeIn",
    "easeOut",
    "easeInOut",
  ];

  it.each(easings)("%s maps 0 → 0 and 1 → 1 monotonically", (name) => {
    const ease = getPathMotionEasing(name);
    expect(ease(0)).toBeCloseTo(0);
    expect(ease(1)).toBeCloseTo(1);

    let previous = ease(0);
    for (let t = 0.05; t <= 1; t += 0.05) {
      const value = ease(t);
      expect(value).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(previous);
      previous = value;
    }
  });

  it("shapes the midpoint as expected", () => {
    expect(getPathMotionEasing("linear")(0.5)).toBeCloseTo(0.5);
    expect(getPathMotionEasing("easeIn")(0.5)).toBeLessThan(0.5);
    expect(getPathMotionEasing("easeOut")(0.5)).toBeGreaterThan(0.5);
    expect(getPathMotionEasing("easeInOut")(0.5)).toBeCloseTo(0.5);
  });
});

describe("normalizePathMotion", () => {
  it("fills in defaults for missing config (legacy paths)", () => {
    expect(normalizePathMotion(undefined)).toEqual(DEFAULT_PATH_MOTION);
    expect(normalizePathMotion({})).toEqual(DEFAULT_PATH_MOTION);
  });

  it("keeps valid values", () => {
    expect(
      normalizePathMotion({
        speed: 2,
        start: 0.25,
        end: 0.75,
        easing: "easeInOut",
      }),
    ).toEqual({ speed: 2, start: 0.25, end: 0.75, easing: "easeInOut" });
  });

  it("rejects non-positive / invalid speeds and unknown easings", () => {
    expect(normalizePathMotion({ speed: 0 }).speed).toEqual(1);
    expect(normalizePathMotion({ speed: -2 }).speed).toEqual(1);
    expect(normalizePathMotion({ speed: NaN }).speed).toEqual(1);
    expect(
      normalizePathMotion({ easing: "bounce" as PathMotionEasing }).easing,
    ).toEqual("linear");
  });

  it("clamps start/end into [0, 1] and never lets them cross", () => {
    expect(normalizePathMotion({ start: -1, end: 2 })).toMatchObject({
      start: 0,
      end: 1,
    });
    // end dragged below start → pushed just past it
    expect(normalizePathMotion({ start: 0.8, end: 0.5 })).toMatchObject({
      start: 0.8,
      end: 0.81,
    });
    // start dragged all the way to the end → leaves room for the min span
    expect(normalizePathMotion({ start: 1, end: 1 })).toMatchObject({
      start: 0.99,
      end: 1,
    });
  });
});

describe("getPathAlignmentOffset honors motion.start", () => {
  const setup = (start: number) => {
    const rectangle = API.createElement({
      type: "rectangle",
      x: 0,
      y: 0,
      width: 100,
      height: 100,
    });
    const points: LocalPoint[] = [pointFrom(0, 0), pointFrom(200, 0)];
    const path = API.createElement({
      type: "path",
      x: 300,
      y: 300,
      width: 200,
      height: 0,
      points,
      targetElementId: rectangle.id,
      motion: { start },
    });
    return { rectangle, path, elementsMap: arrayToMap([rectangle, path]) };
  };

  it("aligns onto the path's first point by default", () => {
    const { rectangle, path, elementsMap } = setup(0);
    // rectangle center (50, 50) → (300, 300)
    expect(getPathAlignmentOffset(path, [rectangle], elementsMap)).toEqual({
      x: 250,
      y: 250,
    });
  });

  it("aligns onto the configured start fraction", () => {
    const { rectangle, path, elementsMap } = setup(0.5);
    // halfway along (300,300)→(500,300) is (400, 300)
    expect(getPathAlignmentOffset(path, [rectangle], elementsMap)).toEqual({
      x: 350,
      y: 250,
    });
  });
});

/** lets the deferred commit in App.componentDidUpdate run */
const flushDeferred = () =>
  act(() => new Promise<void>((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 0)));

const getPath = (id: string) =>
  h.elements.find((el) => el.id === id) as ExcalidrawPathElement;

const getElement = (id: string) =>

type TargetKind = "rectangle" | "ellipse" | "diamond" | "text" | "group";

/**
 * target(s) centered around (50, 50), straight path from (300, 300) to
 * (300 + length, 300) — so a target's center at progress `p` along the path
 * is simply (300 + p * length, 300)
 */
const setup = ({
  length = 400,
  motion,
  target = "rectangle",
}: {
  length?: number;
  motion?: Partial<PathMotionConfig>;
  target?: TargetKind;
} = {}) => {
  let targets: ExcalidrawElement[];
  if (target === "group") {
    targets = [
      API.createElement({
        type: "rectangle",
        x: 0,
        y: 0,
        width: 40,
        height: 100,
        groupIds: ["g1"],
      }),
      API.createElement({
        type: "ellipse",
        x: 60,
        y: 0,
        width: 40,
        height: 100,
        groupIds: ["g1"],
      }),
    ];
  } else if (target === "text") {
    targets = [API.createElement({ type: "text", text: "Hello", x: 0, y: 0 })];
  } else {
    targets = [
      API.createElement({
        type: target,
        x: 0,
        y: 0,
        width: 100,
        height: 100,
        backgroundColor: "#000000",
      }),
    ];
  }

  const points = [pointFrom(0, 0), pointFrom(length, 0)];
  const path = API.createElement({
    type: "path",
    x: 300,
    y: 300,
    ...getSizeFromPoints(points),
    points: points as ExcalidrawPathElement["points"],
    targetElementId: target === "group" ? null : targets[0].id,
    targetGroupId: target === "group" ? "g1" : null,
    motion,
  });
  API.setElements([...targets, path]);
  return { targets, path };
};

const getTargetsCenter = (path: ExcalidrawPathElement) => {
  const elementsMap = h.app.scene.getNonDeletedElementsMap();
  const [minX, minY, maxX, maxY] = getCommonBounds(
    getPathTargetElements(path, elementsMap),
    elementsMap,
  );
  return { x: (minX + maxX) / 2, y: (minY + maxY) / 2 };
};

/**
 * Starts playback of `path` while capturing its per-frame callback instead of
 * letting AnimationController run it on timers, so frames can be stepped by
 * exact amounts of time.
 */
const startPlayback = (path: ExcalidrawPathElement) => {
  let animation: Animation<any> | null = null;
  const spy = vi
    .spyOn(AnimationController, "start")
    .mockImplementation((_key, fn) => {
      animation = fn;
    });
  h.app.pathPlayback.startForPath(getPath(path.id));
  spy.mockRestore();
  expect(animation).not.toBeNull();

  let state = act(() => animation!({ deltaTime: 0, state: undefined }));
  return {
    get totalDuration(): number {
      return state!.totalDuration;
    },
    /** advances playback by `ms`; returns false once it finished */
    step(ms: number) {
      act(() => {
        state = animation!({ deltaTime: ms, state });
      });
      return !!state;
    },
  };
};

const enterEditMode = () => {
  mouse.rightClickAt(400, 300);
  const item = queryByTestId(UI.queryContextMenu()!, "editMotionPath");
  expect(item).not.toBeNull();
  fireEvent.click(item!);
  expect(
    document.querySelector('[data-testid="motion-path-settings"]'),
  ).not.toBeNull();
};

const setSlider = (
  testId: "motion-path-start" | "motion-path-end",
  v: number,
) =>
  fireEvent.change(
    document.querySelector(`[data-testid="${testId}"]`) as HTMLInputElement,
    { target: { value: String(v) } },
  );

beforeEach(async () => {
  localStorage.clear();
  reseed(7);
  mouse.reset();
  AnimationController.reset();
  await render(<Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally={true} />);
});

afterEach(() => {
  vi.restoreAllMocks();
});

describe("movement timing", () => {
  // base speed is 300px/s at the "normal" multiplier
  it.each([
    // [path length, speed, expected ms]
    [300, 0.5, 2000],
    [300, 1, 1000],
    [300, 2, 500],
    [900, 0.5, 6000],
    [900, 1, 3000],
    [900, 2, 1500],
  ])("a %ipx path at %fx speed plays for %ims", (length, speed, expected) => {
    const { path } = setup({ length, motion: { speed } });
    expect(startPlayback(path).totalDuration).toBeCloseTo(expected);
  });

  it("only the configured start..end section counts towards the duration", () => {
    const { path } = setup({ length: 600, motion: { start: 0.25, end: 0.75 } });
    expect(startPlayback(path).totalDuration).toBeCloseTo(1000);
  });
});

describe("motion settings in the edit toolbar", () => {
  it("speed presets set the path's speed multiplier", () => {
    const { path } = setup();
    enterEditMode();

    UI.clickOnTestId("motion-path-speed-fast");
    expect(getPath(path.id).motion.speed).toEqual(2);
    expect(
      document
        .querySelector('[data-testid="motion-path-speed-fast"]')!
        .getAttribute("aria-pressed"),
    ).toBe("true");

    UI.clickOnTestId("motion-path-speed-slow");
    expect(getPath(path.id).motion.speed).toEqual(0.5);

    UI.clickOnTestId("motion-path-speed-normal");
    expect(getPath(path.id).motion.speed).toEqual(1);
  });

  it("changing the speed changes the Test animation duration", () => {
    const { path } = setup({ length: 300 });
    enterEditMode();

    UI.clickOnTestId("motion-path-speed-fast");
    expect(startPlayback(path).totalDuration).toBeCloseTo(500);
  });

  it("the easing select sets the path's easing", () => {
    const { path } = setup();
    enterEditMode();

    fireEvent.change(
      document.querySelector('[data-testid="motion-path-easing"]')!,
      { target: { value: "easeInOut" } },
    );
    expect(getPath(path.id).motion.easing).toEqual("easeInOut");
  });

  it("start/end sliders set the section and re-snap the element onto the start", () => {
    const { path } = setup({ length: 400 });
    enterEditMode();

    setSlider("motion-path-start", 25);
    setSlider("motion-path-end", 75);

    expect(getPath(path.id).motion).toMatchObject({ start: 0.25, end: 0.75 });
    // 25% along (300,300)→(700,300)
    expect(getTargetsCenter(getPath(path.id))).toEqual({ x: 400, y: 300 });
  });

  it("start and end can't cross", () => {
    const { path } = setup();
    enterEditMode();

    setSlider("motion-path-start", 80);
    setSlider("motion-path-end", 50);

    const { start, end } = getPath(path.id).motion;
    expect(start).toBeCloseTo(0.8);
    expect(end).toBeGreaterThan(start);
  });

  it("Reject restores the original motion settings and element position", () => {
    const { path, targets } = setup({ motion: { speed: 2 } });
    enterEditMode();

    UI.clickOnTestId("motion-path-speed-slow");
    setSlider("motion-path-start", 50);
    fireEvent.change(
      document.querySelector('[data-testid="motion-path-easing"]')!,
      { target: { value: "easeIn" } },
    );

    UI.clickOnTestId("motion-path-reject");

    expect(getPath(path.id).motion).toEqual({
      speed: 2,
      start: 0,
      end: 1,
      easing: "linear",
    });
    expect([getElement(targets[0].id).x, getElement(targets[0].id).y]).toEqual([
      0, 0,
    ]);
    expect(h.state.motionPathEditor).toBeNull();
  });

  it("Done keeps the configured settings and the element rests on the start", async () => {
    const { path } = setup({ length: 400 });
    enterEditMode();

    UI.clickOnTestId("motion-path-speed-fast");
    setSlider("motion-path-start", 50);
    UI.clickOnTestId("motion-path-done");
    await flushDeferred();

    expect(h.state.motionPathEditor).toBeNull();
    expect(getPath(path.id).motion).toMatchObject({ speed: 2, start: 0.5 });
    expect(getTargetsCenter(getPath(path.id))).toEqual({ x: 500, y: 300 });
  });
});

describe("playback with configured movement", () => {
  it("travels smoothly from the configured start to the configured end", () => {
    // 400px path, 25%..75% → 200px at 300px/s
    const { path } = setup({ length: 400, motion: { start: 0.25, end: 0.75 } });
    const playback = startPlayback(path);
    const duration = playback.totalDuration;

    expect(getTargetsCenter(path)).toEqual({ x: 400, y: 300 });

    let previousX = 400;
    for (let i = 1; i < 10; i++) {
      playback.step(duration / 10);
      const { x, y } = getTargetsCenter(path);
      expect(x).toBeGreaterThan(previousX);
      expect(x).toBeLessThan(600);
      expect(y).toBeCloseTo(300);
      previousX = x;
    }

    // last frame finishes and puts the element back at its resting start
    expect(playback.step(duration / 10)).toBe(false);
    expect(getTargetsCenter(path)).toEqual({ x: 400, y: 300 });
  });

  it.each([
    // [easing, expected center x at half the duration]
    ["linear", 500], // 0.25 + 0.5 * 0.5   = 0.5    → 300 + 200
    ["easeIn", 425], // 0.25 + 0.125 * 0.5 = 0.3125 → 300 + 125
    ["easeInOut", 500], // symmetric around the midpoint
  ] as const)("applies %s easing", (easing, expectedX) => {
    const { path } = setup({
      length: 400,
      motion: { start: 0.25, end: 0.75, easing },
    });
    const playback = startPlayback(path);

    playback.step(playback.totalDuration / 2);
    expect(getTargetsCenter(path).x).toBeCloseTo(expectedX);
  });

  it("ease out covers more ground early than linear", () => {
    const { path } = setup({ motion: { easing: "easeOut" } });
    const playback = startPlayback(path);

    playback.step(playback.totalDuration / 4);
    // linear would be at 300 + 0.25 * 400 = 400
    expect(getTargetsCenter(path).x).toBeGreaterThan(400);
  });

  it("settings are retained when the animation is played again", () => {
    const { path } = setup({
      length: 400,
      motion: { speed: 2, start: 0.1, end: 0.9, easing: "easeInOut" },
    });

    const run = () => {
      const playback = startPlayback(path);
      const samples = [playback.totalDuration];
      while (playback.step(playback.totalDuration / 8)) {
        samples.push(getTargetsCenter(path).x);
      }
      return samples;
    };

    const first = run();
    const second = run();
    expect(second).toEqual(first);
    expect(getPath(path.id).motion).toEqual({
      speed: 2,
      start: 0.1,
      end: 0.9,
      easing: "easeInOut",
    });
  });

  it.each(["rectangle", "ellipse", "diamond", "text", "group"] as const)(
    "works for a %s target",
    (target) => {
      const { path } = setup({
        target,
        length: 400,
        motion: { start: 0.5, end: 1 },
      });
      const playback = startPlayback(path);

      // aligned onto the configured start point
      const start = getTargetsCenter(path);
      expect(start.x).toBeCloseTo(500);
      expect(start.y).toBeCloseTo(300);

      playback.step(playback.totalDuration / 2);
      const mid = getTargetsCenter(path);
      expect(mid.x).toBeCloseTo(600);
      expect(mid.y).toBeCloseTo(300);
    },
  );
});

describe("persistence", () => {
  it("restores legacy paths without motion settings with defaults", () => {
    const { path } = setup();
    const { motion: _motion, ...legacy } = getPath(path.id);

    const [restored] = restoreElements(
      [legacy as unknown as ExcalidrawPathElement],
      null,
    );
    expect((restored as ExcalidrawPathElement).motion).toEqual({
      speed: 1,
      start: 0,
      end: 1,
      easing: "linear",
    });
  });

  it("keeps saved motion settings and clamps invalid ones", () => {
    const { path } = setup();

    const [kept] = restoreElements(
      [
        {
          ...getPath(path.id),
          motion: { speed: 0.5, start: 0.2, end: 0.6, easing: "easeOut" },
        },
      ],
      null,
    );
    expect((kept as ExcalidrawPathElement).motion).toEqual({
      speed: 0.5,
      start: 0.2,
      end: 0.6,
      easing: "easeOut",
    });

    const [clamped] = restoreElements(
      [
        {
          ...getPath(path.id),
          motion: { speed: -1, start: -0.5, end: 3, easing: "nope" as any },
        },
      ],
      null,
    );
    expect((clamped as ExcalidrawPathElement).motion).toEqual({
      speed: 1,
      start: 0,
      end: 1,
      easing: "linear",
    });
  });
});

I've implemented issue #46 as planned. In the motion-path edit toolbar you can now set speed, easing, and where the element starts and ends on its path. The typecheck passes, the full test suite passes (`yarn test:update`: 122 files, 1728 tests), and `yarn fix` is clean. I haven't tried it in the running app (`yarn start`) or committed anything.

**What it does**

- **Speed:** Slow, Normal and Fast buttons, which make the element move at half, normal or double speed. Normal is the old 300 px/s. The animation takes longer on a longer path, and only the part between start and end counts. That makes "changing the speed changes the duration" hold for any path length.
- **Start and End:** two sliders from 0% to 100% of the path. End always stays ahead of Start. When you move Start, the element jumps to the new start point so you can see where the animation will begin.
- **Easing:** Linear (the default), Ease in, Ease out, or Ease in-out.
- **Playback:** "Test animation" and press-and-hold playback both use these settings, and playing again gives exactly the same motion.
- **Reject and Done:** Reject puts the old settings back and moves the element back to where it was. Done keeps the new settings.
- **Saving:** the settings are saved with the path. Older files that don't have them load with the defaults, and invalid values are corrected on load.

**Main changes**

- `packages/element/src/pathMotion.ts` (new) holds the default settings, the cleanup of bad values, and the easing functions.
- `packages/excalidraw/pathPlayback.ts` now works out the duration from length, speed and the start–end section, then moves the element through that section with the chosen easing.
- `packages/element/src/path.ts`: the function that lines the element up with the path now uses the configured start instead of the first point. Done, the re-snap after resizing or rotating, and playback all go through that function, so they all pick up the new start.
- `packages/excalidraw/actions/actionMotionPathEditor.tsx` has a new action for changing the settings.
- `packages/excalidraw/components/MotionPathEditToolbar.tsx` and its `.scss` file have the new settings panel. Arrow keys used on a slider no longer reach the canvas, so they don't nudge the selected element.

**Tests** are in `packages/excalidraw/tests/pathMotionConfig.test.tsx` and `packages/element/tests/pathMotion.test.ts`. They cover:

- durations for short and long paths at all three speeds;
- each toolbar control, plus Reject and Done;
- smooth movement from start to end, and each easing;
- replaying gives the same result;
- rectangle, ellipse, diamond, text and grouped elements;
- loading old and invalid saved files.

No existing snapshots changed.

**Things to know**

- Each slider change goes into undo history separately, so dragging a slider creates several undo steps. That matches the existing toolbar actions and Excalidraw's own property sliders.
- Changing Start moves the element straight away while you're still editing. Before, the element only moved when you pressed Done. Reject still undoes this.

Do you want me to commit this and add an AI log to the PR, like the #48 PR had?

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-08 04:58:35Z)**_

I fixed the desync: if you move a motion path while it's playing, the element now follows it and comes to rest on the path's start point when playback ends. The typecheck passes, the full test suite passes (1730 tests), and `yarn fix` is clean. I haven't tried it by hand in the running app (`yarn start`) or committed anything.

**Cause:** playback read the path's shape and the element's resting position once, when it started. If the path was dragged partway through, the remaining frames kept moving the element along the path's old position. The last frame then put the element back at its old resting spot, leaving it detached from the moved path.

**Fix** (in `packages/excalidraw/pathPlayback.ts`):

- Every frame now uses the path's current position, so the element rides the path wherever it is.
- When playback ends, the element is put back at its resting spot shifted by however far the path's start point moved. Normally it rests centered on the start point, so it lands right back on the moved path's start, with no trip into edit mode needed. If the path wasn't moved, nothing changes from before.
- Dragging the element itself mid-playback is covered by the same fix, because dragging the element also drags its path.

**Tests:** I added two to `pathMotionConfig.test.tsx`. Each starts playback, drags the path halfway through, and checks that the remaining frames follow the moved path and that the element ends on the new start point. One uses the default start, the other a 25% start. Both failed before the fix and pass now.

While you're dragging, the animation and the drag both move the element. In a real browser that might cause a slight jitter until you let go. The tests step frames directly, so they can't show this.
